title: Common Errors in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Type Errors: Missing annotations, wrong types
Memory Errors: Out of bounds, alignment issues
Synchronization Errors: Missing barriers, race conditions
Compilation Errors: Syntax, imports, JIT issues
code_snippets:
@cute.kernel
def with_sync():
    smem = cute.make_smem_tensor(cute.make_shape(256), cutlass.Float32)
    tid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
    smem[tid] = tid
    cute.arch.syncthreads()
    value = smem[(tid + 1) % 256]
constraints: All kernel parameters must have type annotations
Use CuTe types, not Python types in kernels
Maximum threads per block is 1024 on most GPUs
Block size should be multiple of warp size (32) for efficiency
Ensure all threads in block reach syncthreads()
compressed_summary: This guide addresses common errors encountered while writing CuTe DSL kernels, focusing on type, memory, launch, synchronization, and compilation errors. Type errors often arise from missing annotations or using Python types instead of CuTe types. Memory errors include out-of-bounds access and uninitialized memory, which can be mitigated by bounds checking and proper initialization. Launch configuration errors typically involve exceeding the maximum threads per block or using non-warp-multiple block sizes. Synchronization errors, such as missing syncthreads or conditional sync leading to deadlocks, require careful use of barriers. Compilation errors often stem from incorrect imports or unsupported Python constructs in JIT compilation. Key practices include ensuring type annotations, validating grid/block dimensions, and synchronizing before accessing shared memory. Use validation functions and follow a checklist to prevent errors. Always test with small inputs and carefully analyze error messages for efficient debugging.
